owned_question: How does a compiled semantic library keep 'not known' from collapsing into a definite answer — so that missing data, negative evidence, and unknown each remain distinguishable values that propagate honestly through queries, contracts, and reported numbers?
terms: negative evidence (evidence of absence, asserted false)
non_collapse_laws: NULL differs from zero, from the empty set, and from empty string; silence of an unqueried source is neither zero nor negative evidence.
Under three-valued logic, comparison with an unknown yields unknown, not false: 7 = NULL and 7 <> NULL are both unknown; absence of a row from a filtered result is therefore not evidence of falsity.
Negative evidence must be explicitly asserted (e.g., OWL negative property assertions); under open-world semantics anything not stated is merely unknown, and an unentailed triple is not false.

A numeric result carries its uncertainty with it: publishing a value without its standard uncertainty or interval misreports what is known; truncation by timeout must surface unknown/partial-coverage, not an empty success.

Typed absence cannot be silently unwrapped: a contract carrying Option/Result forces every consumer to branch on absence; implicit coercion of None/Error to a default or zero is prohibited without a declared default at the boundary.
Imputed or defaulted values must be marked as such downstream — an imputed value propagates as imputed (or widened-band), never as observed.

Coverage/completeness travels with results: any aggregate over partial data discloses denominator and coverage fraction; equal treatment of covered and uncovered subpopulations in presentation is forbidden.
carrier_requirements: An uncertain_value carrier pairing value with a band/interval and provenance (observed | imputed | defaulted | inferred), band carried through arithmetic per GUM-style propagation.
An absent-typed carrier (Option-like) for nullable fields, distinct from sentinel values, with no implicit unwrap.
A result/error-typed carrier (Result-like) distinguishing failure from valid absence across API boundaries.
A tri-state boolean outcome (true/false/unknown) with explicit IS UNKNOWN-type inspection instead of coercing unknown to false.
A coverage_report metadata object attached to query/aggregation outputs: rows examined, sources consulted, sources unreachable, time-boundedness (query cutoff).
Provenance tags marking imputation method, default-applied, and deleted-case counts in any analytic output.
operations_or_relations: coalesce_explicit(values..., fallback) — requires caller-visible fallback choice
declared_default(field, default_value, tag=defaulted) — defaulting only at declared boundaries
propagate_uncertainty(combined standard uncertainty per GUM law of propagation)
assert_absence(entity, property) — explicit negative evidence, unlike unstated
open_world_query(q) returns {matches, unknown_completeness: true}; closed_world_query(q) declares CWA posture explicitly
invariants: No operation may map {unknown, absent, inapplicable} onto {0, [], "", false} implicitly.
Every comparison chain through an unknown preserves unknown unless an explicit coalesce/default operator intervenes.
Every published measurement is accompanied by uncertainty or is flagged uncertain-free-by-declaration (never silent).
Aggregate outputs include a coverage report whenever input data was incomplete at collection or query time.
Absence crossing a contract boundary is typed (Option/Result/tri-state), never encoded via sentinels like -1 or NULL-as-magic-value in new contracts.
Closed-world closure (treating not-found as false) occurs only inside operations that name their closed-world posture; open-world consumers receive unknown rather than false.
refusals: Refuse to impute or substitute defaults without recording provenance and surfacing the substitution to downstream consumers.
Refuse to emit 'no results found' for a query whose source list was truncated by timeout/error without marking coverage partial/unknown.
Refuse to report a point estimate without error bars where GUM-applicable inputs were combined numerically.
Refuse to compile nullable-to-nonnullable coercions (implicit unwrap, sentinel coalescing) at internal boundaries.
Refuse to treat lack of assertion as refutation under open-world semantics (no automatic CWA negation).
counterexamples: SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE status <> 'active' excludes rows with status = NULL entirely because status <> 'active' evaluates to unknown — the aggregate quietly reports fewer exceptions than exist; disclosed only if coverage logic distinguishes excluded-unknown rows.

Inverting a sparse feature matrix's zeros as 'user has no interest' confuses unqueried/unobserved entries (unknown) with observed negatives; recommendation scores then launder missing data into negative evidence.

An ETL job times out mid-scan and writes an empty batch; dashboards read '0 events today', converting a truncation failure into confident zero — should have surfaced unknown/partial with a coverage marker.
f(x) = sqrt(mean of measurements X_i) computed and shipped without combining component standard uncertainties; downstream users compare two such numbers as exact when their intervals overlap heavily.
authority_limit: This axis governs representation, propagation, and disclosure of partiality and uncertainty within compiled semantic artifacts (carriers, contracts, query postures, reports). It does not license choosing statistical estimators, setting MAR-vs-MNAR modeling assumptions, defining SQL-standard semantics itself, or adjudicating domain truth; it obligates honest transport of whatever missingness/uncertainty structure the analyst or standard assigns.

sources.title: JCGM 100:2008 — Evaluation of measurement data: Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement (GUM)
sources.note: Free PDF verified on BIPM site; basis for uncertainty-propagation and error-bar obligations (Type A/B evaluation, combined standard uncertainty).

sources.title: Rubin, D.B. (1976). Inference and Missing Data. Biometrika 63(3):581–592
sources.note: MCAR/MAR taxonomy; ignoring-the-mechanism conditions — basis for distinguishing deletion/imputation disclosure duties.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer (W3C Recommendation)
sources.note: Verified quote contrasting closed-world databases with OWL open-world assumption ('may simply be missing... possibly true'); §4.4 negative property assertions as explicit negative evidence.

sources.title: PostgreSQL Documentation §9.2 Comparison Functions and Operators
sources.note: Implementation evidence (not the ISO standard): comparisons with NULL yield unknown; 'Do not write expression = NULL'; IS DISTINCT FROM and IS UNKNOWN predicates.
